Q: Java to display words from my text file in descending order? A:

tl;dr

Files
.readAllLines( Path.of( "/path/to/example.txt" ) )
.stream()              
.flatMap( line -> Arrays.stream( line.split( "\t" ) ) )
.sorted( String.UNICODE_CASEFOLD_ORDER.reversed() )
.toList();

Modern Java

This work is easier using the features of modern Java: NIO.2, lambdas, streams, Sequenced Collections (Java 21+), Comparator, Unicode-compliant case-folding (Java 26+), and IO class (Java 25+).

We can come close to authoring a one-liner that solves this problem.

Write file

Create a file with example data. We use TAB character as field delimiter per your requirements.

try
{
    Files.write(
            Path.of( "/path/to/example.txt" ) ,
            List.of(
                    String.join( "\t" , "Hank" , "Ingrid" , "Jacques" ) ,
                    String.join( "\t" , "Frank" , "Kara" ) ,
                    String.join( "\t" , "Edwina" ) ,
                    String.join( "\t" , "Davis" , "Georgette" , "Alice" ) ,
                    String.join( "\t" , "Bob" , "Carol" )
            )
    );
}
catch ( IOException e ) { throw new RuntimeException( e ); }

Read file

Use Path.of to identify the file location.

Read all the lines from the file into memory, as a List of String objects.

Loop through that list. For each line in the list, split the line by your TAB character delimiter. Calling String#split returns an array of the delimited parts. Then we use Stream#flatMap to send each element of that array (each of our words) separately into the stream.

For good measure, trim & strip each word as another step in the stream. See my Answer for more info.

We need to collect all the words from that stream. You asked to keep duplicates, so we cannot use a Set. We will use a List.

After processing the lines, sort the collected words. For best results across various languages, use the case-folding feature in Java 26+ that follows the sorting rules established by the Unicode Consortium.

You may want to report the final resulting List as a SequencedCollection, its higher super-interface.

try
{
    SequencedCollection < String > words =
            Files
                    .readAllLines(                               // Returns a `List` of `String` objects, one per line read from file. Defaults to UTF-8 character encoding.
                            Path.of( "/path/to/example.txt" )  // Returns a `Path` object.
                    )
                    .stream()                                    // Makes a stream of that list of lines.
                    .flatMap( line ->                            // `.flatMap` enables producing a secondary stream (our words) and sending them individually into the primary stream.
                            Arrays.stream( line.split( "\t" ) )  // Split each line into an array of words. Make a stream of the array’s elements.
                    )
                    .map( String :: trim )                       // Delete extraneous whitespace characters from front and end of each string (each word).
                    .map( String :: strip )
                    .sorted(
                            String.UNICODE_CASEFOLD_ORDER        // Sort the words alphabetically using the Unicode collation order. Accesses a pre-defined `Comparator` object.
                                    .reversed()                  // Reverse the sort order, for a descending sort.
                    )
                    .toList();                                   // Collect the words into a `List`.

    words.forEach( IO :: println );                              // Dump to console.
}
catch ( IOException e ) { throw new RuntimeException( e ); }

Result:

Kara
Jacques
Ingrid
Hank
Georgette
Frank
Edwina
Davis
Carol
Bob
Alice

Q: How to move sidebar to the left in shop pages? A:

Found a workaround... I still don't understand how the default templates work, but I've tried until I give up. I just hard-coded a div style="right;" in the archive-product.php, closing the div just before the sidebar commanding lines. It's crude, I know, but it seems to do the trick.

Q: Return results of an SQL query as JSON in Oracle Database 12c A:

Starting Oracle 19c, the syntax to construct a JSON representation for a row of a table is simplified.

For example: To convert all the rows of the hr.employees to separate JSON files, use:

SELECT JSON_OBJECT(*) FROM hr.employees;

Output:

{
"EMPLOYEE_ID" : 100,
"FIRST_NAME" : "Steven",
"LAST_NAME" : "King",

Q: u'rest_framework' is not a registered namespace A:

i think this bug problem only when you use the auth login inside your app's URL.You need to define the login inside the main url so that it will give the correct url to log in,

so just use the rest_framework.urls inside the main.url page

The account Url should be: /auth/login or /auth/logout/

but when you use it inside your app the url will be:

/yourappname/auth/login or /yourappname/auth/logout

as the data is only stored in this /auth/login/ ,when fected from wrong url it will give the u'rest_framework' is not a registered namespace error
